# Cherie (01, engineer) — BAD-095

## Brief
Add an all-time "First imported" column to the admin /scenes list, put the seven columns in the order Eric asked for, and make Last recorded the default sort.

## Setup, first

`bash scripts/worktree-init.sh` before anything else. Without it tests skip vacuously and nothing starts. Then `npm install` inside `admin/` if `admin/node_modules` is absent.

## The column order

| # | Header | Source |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Scene | `title` (unchanged) |
| 2 | Imported | `libraries` (unchanged) |
| 3 | **First imported** | **new** |
| 4 | Last imported | `last_imported_at` (unchanged) |
| 5 | Users recorded | `users_recorded` (unchanged) |
| 6 | Sessions | `sessions` (unchanged) |
| 7 | Last recorded | `last_recorded_at` — **new default sort, descending** |

Eric wrote the headers in title case; the page uses sentence case ("Users recorded", "Last imported"). Match the page. His list is an order, not a restyling.

The default sort lives in two places that must agree: `listScenes`'s `isSceneSortKey(query.sort) ? query.sort : 'sessions'` in admin/src/lib/scenes.ts, and the page's own fallback in admin/src/app/scenes/page.tsx. Both become `last_recorded`. If they disagree, the header arrow points at one column while the rows are ordered by another.

## The decision this ticket turns on

**First imported is all-time. It is not windowed, and a windowed version answers nothing.**

Every column on /scenes today is inside the `?days=` window. scenes.ts's header comment states it as an invariant — "both CTEs filter on `created_at >= now() - $1 days` before anything is aggregated, so narrowing the window moves these dates rather than revealing older ones" — and `ACQUIRED_CTE` and `RECORDED_CTE` both carry that filter.

A `min(created_at)` over the windowed `acquired` CTE is the oldest acquisition *inside the window*: on the default 30-day view it can never be older than 30 days, so every scene would report a first import inside the last month and the column would rank nothing. Eric asked for this column to find "the oldest most active scenes". A windowed minimum cannot answer that, and on a production 30-day view with recent traffic it looks entirely plausible in a screenshot. That is why this ticket has a reviewer.

So: a **new CTE that reads both acquisition sources with no `created_at` predicate at all**, grouped by the same `lower(btrim(scene_title))` key, producing `min(created_at) as first_imported_at`, left-joined onto `scenes`. The two source halves are the same two `ACQUIRED_CTE` unions: `private.scene_imports` (any `how`) and `private.scene_saves where kind = 'create'`. Same key expression, same `scene_title is not null and btrim(scene_title) <> ''` guard — a different key expression joins to nothing for any title with stray whitespace, and the column is a dash on rows that have a date.

Do not reuse `ACQUIRED_CTE` by parameterising its window. Write the unwindowed one as its own module constant beside it and say in a comment why there are now two: a shared fragment that takes a flag is a fragment somebody widens the windowed half with by accident, which is the failure the existing header comment already guards against.

**This breaks the page's stated invariant, deliberately, and the documentation must say so.** Revise the "the timestamps" section of scenes.ts's header comment: it currently promises every date on the page is inside the window, and after this change exactly one is not. Say which, and say why (the column exists to rank scenes by age, and age does not fit in a window). Whoever reads that comment next must not be able to conclude the unwindowed CTE is a bug.

**A consequence the UI must survive, and should explain in a comment:** a scene first imported two years ago and untouched since shows a real date under First imported and an em dash under both Imported and Last imported on a 30-day window. That is correct and it is the point of the column. Do not coalesce it, do not hide it.

`first_imported_at` is nullable in principle (a scene that reached the page only through `recorded`), so render it through the same `TimeAgo` / `relative` / em-dash treatment the two existing dates use, and type it `string | null` on `SceneRow`. Give it a `SORTS` entry so its header sorts; the order clause already appends `nulls last`.

## Performance — read admin/CLAUDE.md before you write the query

This page has a documented history of exactly the failure this change risks. `admin/src/lib/db.ts` pools **three** connections; a render that asks for more wedges until Cloud Run kills it at 300s; `test/server/admin-pool.test.mjs` fails the build if any file under `admin/src` starts concurrent promises. Migrations 0010 and 0011 added bare `(created_at desc)` indexes because whole-table time windows were sequentially scanning and returning 504s in production on 2026-08-20.

An unwindowed `min(created_at) group by lower(btrim(scene_title))` over the whole of `scene_imports` and `scene_saves` is a full scan of both, and **no `(created_at desc)` index helps it** — there is no index on the key expression. It also cannot be restricted to the page's 50 rows, because sorting by First imported has to order the whole result set before paging.

Required of you:

- It stays **one round trip**. The new CTE composes into the existing `with` clause of both `listScenes` and `countScenes`. It does not become a second `sql.unsafe` and it does not become a `Promise.all`. The existing one-round-trip test must keep passing and must not become vacuous.
- Reason about the cost against the real table sizes and **write what you found into the comment**, with the number you based it on. If an index on `lower(btrim(scene_title))` is warranted, that is a SQL migration — the `server-changes` skill, deployed from CI — and it is **out of scope**: file it with `proposal file` rather than widening this ticket. Do not write a migration here.
- Never add a second concurrent query to work around it.

## The tests

`test/server/admin-scenes-list.test.mjs` is text assertions over the dashboard's own source. Read its head comment first — it says plainly what it does and does not prove (not that the SQL is valid, not that it runs). Extend that file; do not start a new one.

Two existing tests fail by design and must be updated, not deleted: `the empty row spans every column the header declares` asserts `headers === 6`, and `colSpan` must follow it to 7.

Add, in the shape of what is there:

- `first_imported` names a column the query actually selects — the same guard the two existing sort keys get. An `order by` on a column no CTE produced is a 500 on the first header click, not a build error.
- The first-import aggregate is a `min` over the **unwindowed** CTE. Assert both halves: that it is `min(created_at)`, **and** that the CTE it sits in carries no `created_at >= now()` predicate. A test that only checks for `min(...)` passes against the windowed version, which is the exact mistake this ticket exists to prevent. Build the windowed version first and confirm your test fails on it — a test that passes both ways is worth nothing here.
- `listScenes` carries `firstImportedAt` onto the row through `iso()`, and `SceneRow` declares it `string | null`.
- The seven `<Th>` headers appear in Eric's **sequence** in the source, not merely that each exists. The visible half of this ticket is the order.
- The default sort is `last_recorded` in both places, and they agree.

## Ticket proposals
- **Expression index on lower(btrim(scene_title)) for the two acquisition tables** — suggested P3; created as [[BAD-096]] at P3 by Spud.
  Why: BAD-095 adds an unwindowed min(created_at) grouped by lower(btrim(scene_title)) over private.scene_imports and private.scene_saves, to power the admin /scenes First imported column. It is the only query on that page that scans whole tables rather than a window, and it cannot be narrowed: sorting by First imported must order every scene before the page's 50 rows are taken. No existing index covers the key expression, so the plan is two sequential scans into a HashAggregate. Affordable now and deliberately left alone in BAD-095 (a migration is out of that ticket's scope and deploys from CI), but it is the first thing on this page that gets slower while the window stays the same width.
  Evidence: Indexes present: scene_imports_created_at_idx (created_at desc) and scene_imports_lower_created_at_idx (lower(email), created_at desc) from migrations 0010; scene_saves has (lower(email), created_at desc) 0003, a bucket index 0006 and (created_at desc) 0011. None is on the title expression. Measured with explain (analyze, buffers) against the local stack (653 scene_imports, 2639 scene_saves): HashAggregate, two Seq Scans, 56 shared buffer hits, 1.076 ms. That is ~0.3 us/row, so a million acquisition rows is a few hundred ms on one of the three connections admin/src/lib/db.ts pools — under Cloud Run's 300s ceiling but the point where the index earns its keep. admin/CLAUDE.md records a real 504 on 2026-08-20 from unindexed whole-table scans on this dashboard.
